title: Branch Coverage
definition: Branch coverage measures whether tests exercise the relevant outcomes of control-flow branches.
purpose: Reveal conditional paths that have not been executed by the current test set.
history: Structural testing uses control-flow representations and coverage measures to observe which program paths tests exercise.
mental_model: Place a checkpoint on every possible exit from each decision and choose inputs that reach every checkpoint.
analogy: Checking every doorway confirms each can be reached; it does not prove everything inside each room is correct.
industry_notes: Coverage is evidence about execution, not an oracle for correct requirements or assertions.
ai_notes: AI may claim complete testing after one successful example; require explicit branch-to-input mapping.
interview_notes: Ask for minimum inputs covering an if/else-if chain and the limitations of 100 percent coverage.
exercise_candidates: Select one input per reachable branch
lab_candidates: Map shipping table columns to executed branches
